summary_hint: <Boarder> pays <borrower> $<amount> <frequency> for room at <property address>, with a payment history running <period>.

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity/source — who produced the record (borrower ledger, property manager)

typed_core.name: borrower_recipient_name
typed_core.why: identity — attributes receipt to the borrower (flattened from person)

typed_core.name: relationship_to_borrower
typed_core.why: processor — boarder-income eligibility depends on the relationship

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity/linkage — the shared residence; must match subject (flattened from address)

typed_core.name: agreement_start_date
typed_core.why: processor — establishes length of the arrangement

typed_core.name: agreement_end_date
typed_core.why: processor — whether the arrangement is ongoing through closing

typed_core.name: written_agreement_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — whether a written lease exists (degraded from boolean)

typed_core.name: monthly_or_periodic_payment_amount
typed_core.why: processor — the boarder-income figure (money stays string, coerced to Decimal)

typed_core.name: payment_frequency
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the amount is meaningless without its frequency (degraded from enum)

typed_core.name: payment_due_day_or_schedule
typed_core.why: processor — schedule detail for reconciling receipts

typed_core.name: total_payments_received
typed_core.why: processor — cross-check against the payment history sum
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture this stated total verbatim; do not compute an average or a stability judgment.

typed_core.name: current_arrears
typed_core.why: processor — arrears undercut a 'stable receipt' conclusion

typed_core.name: recipient_account_last4
typed_core.why: PII (restricted, pre-masked) — the deposit account receiving payments
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the deposit account last-4 (the account receiving payments).

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: linkage — attaches document to the loan file (confidential identifier)

nested_lists.name: payment_history
nested_lists.shape_reason: a 1-2 year history can carry 24+ entries and per-field wrapping risks the 16,384-token ceiling

fields.name: date
fields.why: processor establishes stable receipt and matches deposits

fields.name: method
fields.why: processor — how the payment was made (ledger/check/deposit)

fields.name: status
fields.why: processor — each payment status; a returned/late status undercuts stability

rejected.name: average_monthly_payment_received, late_or_missed_payment_count
rejected.reason: derived conclusions — rules/tags compute these from payment_history; tags describe, rules judge

rejected.name: party_names / party_addresses
rejected.reason: generic; superseded by typed payer/recipient names and property_address

encoding_variations: The payment amount may be stated as monthly, weekly, or per-period; payment_frequency beside monthly_or_periodic_payment_amount is the required disambiguator (a $600 weekly figure != $600 monthly).
Receipt evidence may be a borrower-kept ledger, cancelled checks, or bank-statement deposits; issuer_name and the supporting-document list disambiguate the source's independence.

open_questions.q: Two candidate lists — payment_history (chosen) vs supporting_bank_statements_or_checks. Budget is one list per document.
options: keep payment_history as the nested list
open_questions.recommendation: keep payment_history as the nested list; flatten supporting evidence to a bare string list only if a consumer appears GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: total_payments_received as fact vs conclusion — it is a stated total on the document (fact) but close to a computed figure.
open_questions.recommendation: keep it (stated figure, disambiguated by the history rows); reject only the average and the missed-payment count, which are judgments

notes: No rules read this document today, so there is no rule floor; fields earn their place on identity, PII protection, or processor review.
Prompt hint (doc-level): this is a boarder-income document — the reviewer wants stable, documented receipt into the borrower's account.
Prompt hint (doc-level): do not compute an average or a stability judgment; average_monthly_payment_received is a derived conclusion — omitted. Money values stay strings in value (e.g. '600.00').
PII: recipient_account_last4 (pre_masked true) needs _PII_FIELDS registration; loan_number is a confidential identifier flagged for review.
Ambiguity: loan_number's why is 'linkage', not one of the five reason classes; classified as identity (attaches/cross-references the loan file).
